title: Veterans Pension Rate Redetermination — Insurance Premium Reports and Their Age
content:
# Insurance premiums in a redetermined Veterans Pension rate

In a redetermination of the annual Veterans Pension, insurance premiums count by how recently they were reported, the medical expense reports on the award being aged in whole months from receipt to the redetermination:

1. Medical expense reports received 3 to 11 whole months before the redetermination count as premiums at their total.
2. When none was received in that span and some were received 12 to 23 whole months before, the standard Medicare Part B premium of 202.90 a month for 12 months, for each member of the household the rate category covers, is counted instead — 2 members where the category counts spouse income, 1 where it does not.
3. Otherwise premiums add nothing.

| Household members | Standard premium counted |
|---|---|
| 1 | 202.90 times 12, which is 2434.80 |
| 2 | 202.90 times 12 times 2, which is 4869.60 |

### Boundary readings (hypothetical reports)

- A report received 11 whole months before counts at its amount; one received 12 whole months before does not count at its amount and, when no report was received 3 to 11 whole months before, brings in the standard premium — whether or not other reports were received fewer than 3 whole months before.
- A report received 23 whole months before brings in the standard premium; at 24 whole months it no longer does, and premiums add nothing.
